clinical_notes: CheckMate 017/057 studied nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks versus docetaxel, after platinum. Fixed-dose q14/q28 and SC schedules are supported through dosing/formulation bridging, not separate randomised superiority estimates. The pooled lung results do not establish benefit for other tumours or first-line, perioperative or small-cell lung settings.
The four-weekly nivolumab source requires thyroid tests before each cycle and when clinically indicated; do not borrow the separate monthly wording from the two-weekly regimen.

lanes.label: Bloods and organ safety
cells: Blood count, kidney and liver tests, glucose and thyroid tests; review autoimmune conditions, transplants, previous immune reactions and all current medicines. BRAF tumour status is checked for the advanced or adjuvant melanoma indication.

Blood count, kidney/liver tests and glucose before every 4-week cycle. Thyroid function is checked before each cycle and when clinically indicated. Cortisol and other tests are added when clinically indicated. Report new symptoms at every visit and between visits; normal blood results do not rule out immune toxicity.
Contact the team for new symptoms; extra tests may be needed between scheduled checks.
Safety bloods do not by themselves show whether cancer is responding.

Continue immune-toxicity monitoring for at least five months after the last dose, and longer when advised. Keep any prescribed steroid taper, hormone replacement and specialist follow-up. Scans follow your individual disease plan.

milestones.title: Ongoing treatment and review
milestones.why: Nivolumab helps immune cells act against melanoma that cannot be completely removed or has spread. The aim is disease control; benefit and side effects are reviewed for you.
milestones.clinical: Nivolumab is given as 480 mg by IV infusion over 60 minutes OR 1200 mg by subcutaneous injection over 3–5 minutes, on Day 1 every 4 weeks. Allow extra time for assessment, preparation and observation. The team selects one formulation. A subcutaneous injection is given into the thigh or abdomen, alternating sites and avoiding damaged skin, scars or moles. IV and subcutaneous doses are not interchangeable milligram for milligram. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, with individual benefit and safety review.
milestones.action: Confirm the current phase, prescription, tests and support plan.

clinical_notes: Nivolumab every 4 weeks. Treatment continues until progression or unacceptable toxicity, with individual benefit and safety review.

If a visit is missed or treatment is held, contact the unit for a new plan. Do not count a missed appointment as a dose received. An interval change, operation or new phase does not erase earlier immune toxicity or a permanent-stop decision.

Blood count, kidney/liver tests and glucose before every 4-week cycle. Thyroid function is checked before each cycle and when clinically indicated. Cortisol and other tests are added when clinically indicated. Report new symptoms at every visit and between visits; normal blood results do not rule out immune toxicity.
Routine dose reductions are not recommended for these immunotherapies. The clinician may hold or stop treatment and treat the immune effect.

If changing from two-weekly to four-weekly nivolumab, the first four-weekly dose is two weeks after the last two-weekly dose. For the reverse change, the first two-weekly dose is four weeks after the last four-weekly dose. The team confirms the formulation and dates.
